clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with a 5-month history of bilateral asymptomatic erythematous infiltrating nodules (2×3 cm) in the axillae and trunk, accompanied by constitutional symptoms (asthenia, anorexia, 10 kg weight loss). Clinical breast examination revealed no palpable masses. Skin biopsy confirmed metastatic undifferentiated carcinoma with immunohistochemistry showing ER+ (50% of cells, ++/+++ intensity), PR-, and HER2- phenotype, consistent with mammary origin. Laboratory studies revealed elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 98 mm/hour) and tumor markers (CA 15-3 >500 U/mL, CEA 6.37 ng/mL). The patient was referred to oncology and initiated on palbociclib 125 mg with aromatase inhibitor therapy. Although cutaneous lesions resolved, tumor markers (CA 15-3 and CEA) continued to rise at 3 months post-treatment initiation, indicating ongoing disease progression. The patient died 7 months after diagnosis of the cutaneous metastases from primary breast carcinoma.
